metadata.title: The Well-Tempered clAIvier
metadata.subtitle: Prelude IV in C-sharp minor (third edition)
metadata.credits: Bars 19-20 (R.H.): J. S. Bach, WTC I, Fugue in C-sharp minor BWV 849, subject 1 (C#-B#-E-D#)

notes: 1 i: M; L broken C#m, turning to V
2 descent
3 M again; L through A to the leading-tone chord
4 i - VI
5 IMITATION: L states M (tenor); R answers on the and of 2, on the dominant
6 answer completes over V7; V - i in root position at 2.5
7 V: M on the dominant
8 i, then B7 (V of E)
9 I: M in E
10 IMITATION in E: L leads, R answers on the dominant
11 the answer completes over B7
12 I - vi; L walks in eighths
13 I - IV - V7 (4-3 over B)
14 V7 - vi - I7 (D natural)
15 A major: M
16 IMITATION in F#m: L leads, R answers on C#7 (the falling-thirds chain is broken)
17 answer completes; C#7 - D (VI of F#m, Neapolitan of C#m)
18 B major: M; turns to G#m7 so the C# can be held
19 V pedal. CRUX (BWV 849) C#-B#: 4-3 over G#; the L.H. leaves the B# to the R.H.
20 CRUX E-D#: i6/4 - V7 over the pedal (6-5)
21 ARRIVAL: held seventh F#5 over V(b9) - V7
22 DROP: M in diminution; i6/4 - V - V7 over the pedal
23 flurry: V - i - iv
24 hemiola (L in groups of eight)
25 hemiola
26 V7 approach
27 RETURN on root-position i (the bar-1 left hand returns)
28 V: M on the dominant
29 L states M in the tenor, R figures C#m (no A against the motif's G#)
30 Neapolitan sixth
31 French sixth A-C#-D#-F## (F## only in the R.H.)
32 cadential 6/4 - V7 (the 6/4 now reaches its dominant)
33 i: STRUCTURAL CADENCE on C#3; M with rising tail
34 LAMENT BASS in quarters: A - G# - G
36 V7: M on the dominant
37 closing tetrachord over i - iv6 - V7 (6-5 on beat 3)
38 final tonic
